note: Official claim process, claim windows, compensation limits and escalation route for the carriers covered by the Delivery Problems triage, from each carrier's own terms/claims pages where directly accessible. Several large carrier sites block automated fetching; in those cases the figures are drawn from a web search whose results quote/paraphrase the same official URL (cited), and this is flagged per-carrier in 'source_access_note'. Null = could not verify; listed in 'unverified'.

carriers.name: Royal Mail
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: Royal Mail allows the sender to claim; for a retail purchase the SENDER is normally the retailer, not the consumer receiving it — the consumer's direct claim right applies mainly when the consumer themselves was the sender (e.g. a return they posted).
carriers.claim_process: Online inland claim via Royal Mail's Claims Centre, or by post using the inland claims form; requires proof of posting and proof of value.

claim_windows.loss: Within 80 calendar days of posting (30 days for Tracked 24/Tracked 48).
claim_windows.damage_or_part_loss: Within 80 calendar days of posting (30 days for Tracked 24/Tracked 48).

compensation_limits.1st_class: Up to £20 for contents, plus postage refund
compensation_limits.2nd_class: Up to £20 for contents, plus postage refund
compensation_limits.special_delivery_guaranteed_by_1pm: Up to £750 included; up to £2,500 with purchased extra compensation
compensation_limits.special_delivery_guaranteed_by_9am: Up to £50 included; up to £2,500 with purchased extra compensation

carriers.escalation_route: POSTRS (Postal Redress Service, run by CEDR, Ofcom-approved) — free, after Royal Mail issues a final response or after a reasonable wait with no resolution (6-8 week typical timeline once a complaint is accepted).
carriers.source_access_note: royalmail.com's own compensation-policy pages returned a 403 (bot-blocked) on direct automated fetch; the figures above are drawn from a web search whose results quote text directly from those same official URLs, not from a third-party aggregator.

carriers.name: Evri
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: Evri's claims process is for its own customer (normally the retailer who booked the delivery), not the end recipient. Confirmed: Evri is NOT a POSTRS member (POSTRS covers Royal Mail only) — no ADR/ombudsman scheme found for Evri.
carriers.claim_process: Via the Evri account of whoever booked the parcel; Evri's own terms direct complainants to its 'Contact Us' page, with no published ADR scheme.

claim_windows.loss_or_damage_or_late: Recommended within 28 days for UK services, 45 days for international services (mandatory for business customers; described as a recommendation, not an explicit hard deadline, for consumers in the T&Cs we read).

compensation_limits.enhanced_cover: Up to £999 (purchased at time of booking, by the sender only)

carriers.escalation_route: No ADR/ombudsman scheme found. For a consumer, the realistic escalation is via the RETAILER who chose Evri (see scenarios.json), since Evri's own complaints route has no binding independent scheme confirmed.

carriers.name: DPD
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: DPD's terms and conditions govern the relationship with whoever booked the parcel (normally the retailer), not the end recipient.
carriers.claim_process: Notify DPD in writing; DPD's own T&Cs (Condition 11 'Liability for loss and damage', Condition 12 'Extended Cover', Condition 13 'Claims for compensation').

claim_windows.final_deadline: One year from the dispatch date.

compensation_limits.expresspak_parcel_freight_parcel_shop_pa: £100 per item (or actual value if lower)
compensation_limits.extended_cover: Up to £5,000 per consignment or £15/kg (whichever is lower), minimum £100 per shipment — purchasable by the sender only

carriers.escalation_route: No ADR/ombudsman scheme found for DPD specifically (not a POSTRS member). Escalation realistically runs via the retailer who chose DPD.

carriers.name: Yodel
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: Yodel's claims process is for whoever booked the parcel (normally the retailer). Note: Yodel's consumer-facing sending brand, Yodel Direct, has moved to inpostdirect.co.uk (confirmed via a permanent redirect from yodeldirect.co.uk), reflecting Yodel's commercial link with InPost.
carriers.claim_process: Via the account of whoever booked the parcel (log in, 'Create claim').

claim_windows.damage_or_part_loss: Within 14 days of delivery (as reported by a web search citing Yodel's own guidance; we could not independently confirm this exact figure on an official Yodel page after the Yodel Direct rebrand).
claim_windows.never_arrived: 28 days from collection (same caveat as above).

carriers.escalation_route: No ADR/ombudsman scheme found for Yodel.
carriers.source_access_note: The Yodel Direct terms URL now permanently redirects to inpostdirect.co.uk; we confirmed the £50 standard-cover figure on the redirected page itself, but could not independently re-confirm the 14-day/28-day claim-window figures on an official page after this rebrand — flagged as lower-confidence in 'unverified'.

carriers.name: UPS
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: UPS's claims process is designed for its own shipping customer (normally the retailer), not the end recipient of a retail parcel.

claim_windows.lost: Up to 9 months from the shipment date.

compensation_limits.declared_value: Up to $50,000 per package, for an additional fee

carriers.escalation_route: No ombudsman; dispute is with UPS directly or, for the consumer, via the retailer who chose UPS.
carriers.source_access_note: ups.com returned an access-denied response on direct automated fetch; figures are drawn from a web search citing that same official URL.

carriers.name: FedEx
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: FedEx's claims process is designed for its own shipping customer (normally the retailer).
carriers.claim_process: Online via the FedEx Customer Support claims portal.

claim_windows.damaged_or_missing_contents_domestic: Within 60 calendar days of the shipment date.
claim_windows.damaged_or_missing_contents_internationa: Within 21 calendar days of the shipment date.
claim_windows.undelivered_or_lost: Within 9 months of the shipment date.

compensation_limits.default_domestic_express: $100 declared-value liability included at no extra cost
compensation_limits.declared_value: Up to $50,000 per package for most commodities, for an additional fee

carriers.escalation_route: No ombudsman; dispute is with FedEx directly or via the retailer who chose FedEx.

carriers.name: DHL
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: DHL's claims process is designed for its own shipping customer (normally the retailer).
carriers.claim_process: Written claim submission to DHL (DHL Express Claims Guide); figures vary materially by service (Express vs eCommerce) and mode (air/road/sea).

claim_windows.dhl_express_general: Within 30 days of DHL accepting the shipment.
claim_windows.dhl_ecommerce: Within 90 days of the original ship date.

compensation_limits.international_air_default: Capped per kilogram under the Montreal Convention (approx. 22 Special Drawing Rights/kg, roughly $23 USD/kg at the exchange rate checked) rather than by declared value, unless the shipper purchased Shipment Insurance covering full declared value.

carriers.escalation_route: No ombudsman; dispute is with DHL directly or via the retailer who chose DHL.
carriers.source_access_note: The official DHL Express Claims Guide PDF could not be parsed by our automated fetch (returned as unreadable binary/compressed streams); the figures above are drawn from a web search whose results describe that same official document, not from an independently-read copy of the PDF text. The exact $/kg conversion is lower-confidence — flagged in 'unverified'.

carriers.name: USPS
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: USPS's claims process can be filed by either the sender or (for some cases) the recipient with the mailer's permission, depending on the specific USPS guidance — we treated this as more directly accessible to a consumer than the private couriers above, but did not fully verify every edge case.
carriers.claim_process: Online at usps.com within the applicable window, with proof of value and tracking information.

claim_windows.priority_mail_and_other_insured: File no earlier than 15 days, no later than 60 days, from the mailing date.
claim_windows.priority_mail_express: File no earlier than 7 days from the mailing date.
claim_windows.damaged_or_missing_contents: May file immediately; must file no later than 60 days after the mailing date.

carriers.escalation_route: No ombudsman; USPS has its own internal appeals process for a denied claim (not independently verified here).

carriers.name: Amazon Logistics
carriers.note_on_direct_claims: There is no separate 'claim against Amazon Logistics' process for consumers the way there is for UPS/FedEx — Amazon Logistics is Amazon's own delivery arm. A buyer's claim is made against Amazon/the seller via Amazon's own A-to-z Guarantee (for third-party-seller orders) or Amazon's standard customer service (for orders sold and fulfilled by Amazon itself, which is NOT covered by the A-to-z Guarantee).
carriers.claim_process: Via 'Your Orders' > the relevant order > 'File/View Claim', for third-party-seller purchases only. For a third-party-seller order, you must first contact the seller and allow 2 business days for a response before Amazon will consider an A-to-z Guarantee claim.

claim_windows.a_to_z_guarantee_eligibility: The order's last possible (estimated) delivery date must be 90 days or less before the claim.
claim_windows.never_received: Can file once 3 days have passed since the latest estimated delivery date, or once tracking shows a delivery confirmation you dispute, whichever is sooner.

compensation_limits.a_to_z_guarantee: Up to $2,500 (as reported by a web search citing Amazon's own help page).

carriers.escalation_route: No external ombudsman found; Amazon's own A-to-z Guarantee decision is the final internal step we could verify.
carriers.source_access_note: amazon.com's own help page returned a 503 (temporarily unavailable) on direct automated fetch; figures are drawn from a web search whose results quote/paraphrase that same official page.

unverified.reason: Not stated as a fixed figure on the official page we could access.

Figures (14 days / 28 days) could not be independently re-confirmed on an official page after Yodel Direct's redirect to inpostdirect.co.uk; kept (not nulled) because they are drawn from a web search citing Yodel's own prior guidance, but flagged here as lower-confidence rather than presented as fully primary-source-verified.

The official DHL Express Claims Guide PDF could not be parsed directly; the ~22 SDR/kg (~$23/kg) figure is drawn from a web search describing that document, not independently read from the PDF text itself. Kept with this caveat rather than nulled, since the underlying Montreal Convention SDR/kg mechanism itself is independently well-established.
